guidance:
# Cell-Tracking Agent Guidance

**Avoid overly strict detection thresholds in early timepoints (t=0–71):** Only ~4–12 cells are present and well-separated; the detector must not discard dim or slightly diffuse cells as noise, or you will miss the seed population and break downstream tracking. 

**Expect rapid density escalation and crowding artifacts from t=107 onward:** Cell overlap increases sharply; by t=213–249 the monolayer is near-confluent. The detector will struggle to resolve individual cell boundaries in dense regions — do *not* chase perfect completeness in late frames, as this will generate false positives (cell debris, halos, contact shadows) and destabilize tracks. Instead, prioritize recall in sparse-to-moderate phases (t=0–142) where cells are still resolvable.

**The Z-dimension (35 planes, 1 µm spacing) is coarse relative to XY (90 nm):** Cells flatten significantly over time; signal centroid will drift in Z. Ensure the linking model permits modest axial movement and does not penalize Z-displacements too heavily, or you will lose tracks during the morphological transition from t=71 to t=142.

**Patch-size tiling risk: MODERATE–HIGH.** Current 384×384 on a 708×512 XY plane produces 2 tiles in X and 1–2 in Y, creating visible seams. Recommend **368×368** (multiples of 16, no resize needed) to distribute boundaries more uniformly and reduce periodic edge artifacts in sparse regions. Z-patches (24 of 35) are safe; no change needed there.

**Self-training caution: Set a realistic completeness target.** True achievable recall at t=213–249 is likely ~0.6–0.7 (crowded monolayer; individual cells not fully resolvable). Chasing the default 0.8 will waste 2–3 refinement rounds and risk detector overfitting to noise. Reduce **max_rounds to 2** and **target to 0.65** to focus effort on sparse–moderate timepoints where gains are real.
